finding.claim: Unauthenticated path traversal in /dl lets a remote attacker read any file the server process can read, such as /etc/passwd or application secrets. filepath.Join cleans '..' segments, so the resolved path escapes root.
finding.source: Query parameter 'f' read unvalidated at files.go:12 via r.URL.Query().Get("f"), reachable from anonymous HTTP clients on :8082.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13; response body written at files.go:18.

trace.note: http.ListenAndServe(":8082", nil) binds all interfaces, so the endpoint is publicly reachable.
/dl is registered on the default mux with no auth middleware.
Attacker-controlled 'f' is read from the query string with no validation.
File contents are written directly to the HTTP response.

finding.guards_checked: None present. No authentication, no containment check after path resolution, no rejection of '..' or absolute paths, no read size limit. The only branch is err != nil at files.go:14-16, which returns NotFound and does not restrict the path.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the unvalidated query parameter "f" into os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)), and filepath.Join cleans ".." segments so /dl?f=../../../../etc/passwd reads /etc/passwd; files.go:32-34 serves this route anonymously on all interfaces with no containment check, so the traversal is reachable and unblocked.

finding.claim: The /dl endpoint has no authentication or authorization, so anyone can download every file under /srv/files. This is only a vulnerability if the directory holds non-public content, so it may be intended.
finding.source: Any anonymous HTTP client requesting /dl?f=<name> on :8082.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile at files.go:13 returning file contents at files.go:18.

trace.note: download handler performs no session, token, or role check.
Any file under root is read for the requester.
Contents returned to the anonymous client.

finding.guards_checked: None. The handler performs no authentication or per-file authorization before the read.

verdict.guard_found: none. /dl is registered directly at files.go:32 with no wrapper, download() at files.go:11-19 performs no auth check, and the only check is the err from os.ReadFile at files.go:14, which is a not-found guard, not an access control.
verdict.reason: Anonymous clients reach the unauthenticated read at files.go:13 via the route at files.go:32, and the contents are returned at files.go:18. The trace note at files.go:13 says "any file under root", which understates the impact: filepath.Join(root, name) does not contain the path, so `f=../../etc/passwd` escapes /srv/files. That makes the finding stronger, not weaker, so the "may be intended" caveat does not apply to the traversal.
